lines.text: Frank Kowalski retires on a Thursday, with a certificate from Aletheion that thanks him for thirty-seven years of service in a font chosen to look like handwriting, and a party in the Kowalskis’ flat that overflows into the corridor and takes the plant pot with it.

Half the courier quarter is there. Halsey sends a message, which Frank reads aloud, and which is three sentences long and makes Eleanor cry. Amanda has taken the afternoon off, which she tells you she has never done, with the slightly dazed air of someone who has just discovered it is possible.
Abbott. Jack. Come here. I want to say something and I’ve had two of Eleanor’s drinks, so it’ll come out wrong.
I said I wanted to leave something in that outfit that wasn’t tonnage. I did. It’s you. Don’t argue, I’m retired, I outrank everybody.

choices.text: “You taught me where the holes were. I’ve not fallen in one yet.”

lines.text: You have never hugged anyone. You discover that your body knows how, that it has been waiting four years for somebody to be hugged, and that Frank Kowalski is built for the job.
All right. All right. Eleanor, he’s hugging me, you owe me a drink, I said he was a hugger.
I said he was a hugger. You said he was a two-second hold station.

You’ve fallen in two. You climbed out. That’s the only version of not falling in that exists, son. Now go and talk to my granddaughter before she takes another afternoon off and the facility collapses.

Later, when the corridor has gone quiet and the plant pot has been righted, you find Eleanor on the balcony that is not really a balcony, a window alcove with two chairs in it, looking out at the station’s ring.
He’ll be impossible for a month. Then he’ll find something to fix. There’s always something to fix.

You know what I’ve lived in, Jack? Mining habitats, corporate housing, a station flat, and for eleven months a converted freighter that Frank swore was temporary. Home was never any of them. Home is where that idiot is, and where Amanda is safe. Home is where you don’t have to be somebody else.
She looks at you when she says the last part. She has always known. You have always known she knew.

choices.text: “I don’t know what that’s like. Being somewhere I don’t have to be somebody else.”
“Thank you for the stew. All of it. Every time.”

lines.text: I know you don’t. That’s why you keep bringing the container back. One day you’ll tell us who you are, or you won’t, and either way the stew’s the same. That’s what home is. It doesn’t ask.
You sit with her until the ring has turned all the way round once. Neither of you says anything else. Nothing else is needed.
You’re welcome. Bring the container back. That’s the rule, and the rule’s the whole point.

Amanda walks you to the courier ring. The station is on its night cycle and the corridors are empty, and she holds your hand in them in a way that would have been unthinkable to the boy who arrived at Callisto, and is now simply what happens.

They’re going to stay here. Both of them. Grandad says the pension stretches further on Nexus than anywhere, and Gran says the plant likes it. So this is where home is, now. For them. For me, as long as the facility has me.
I’m telling you so that you know where to come back to. Whatever you are when you come back.

You kiss her at the ring, with ALC-7293 behind you and the whole of a station full of people you love in front, and you fly back to Callisto with the feeling, for the first time, of leaving somewhere rather than arriving.
Callisto in two jumps.
Jack. Hold onto that. All of it. Whatever happens next, hold onto where they are.
It is not a hint. There is no contract. It is the nearest thing to a warning that she has been able to give you in four years, and you hear it, and you do not yet know what it is warning you about.
